newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Commerzbank profit disappoints, shares fall.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Commerzbank profit disappoints, shares fall.

text.p: Shares in Germany's Commerzbank AG fell three percent on Tuesday after it disappointed investors with a lower-than-expected 22 percent rise in net profit last year.

Both Commerzbank and its larger rival Deutsche Bank AG also said they were keeping their dividends for 1996 unchanged at 1.35 marks and 1.80 marks respectively per five-mark share, largely as expected.
Deutsche released no earnings figures and will publish first results for 1996 in late February.
It is expected to report stagnant 1996 profit due to the cost of compensating investors for alleged mismanagement at its London funds unit Morgan Grenfell Asset Management(MGAM).
Commerzbank said 1996 net profit rose to approximately 1.19 billion marks ($719.2 million) from 979 million, well below analysts' forecasts for a rise of more than 30 percent to 1.3 billion marks.
The news spurred a bout of profit-taking in German banking stocks, now seen overvalued after having been among the top performers in the stock market's rally this year.
"The market was waiting for an opportunity to take profits and they got it today," said Stefan Ermisch, banking analyst at WestLB in Duesseldorf.
Matthew Czepliewicz, banking analyst at Salomon Brothers in London, said: "German banks have had an extremely good run, we feel the big banks have now overshot their fair valuation."
Shares in Commerzbank closed down 1.40 marks or 3.2 percent at 42.40 marks. The closing share price was still up 9.4 percent from the first trading day of 1997.

Christine Winkler, an analyst at Hypo-Bank in Munich, said she had lowered her recommendation for Commerzbank shares to short-term underperform for this week from neutral. But she still recommends holding the stock in the longer term.
Deutsche shares ended down 1.85 marks or 2.2 percent at 83.30 marks, still up 16 percent from the beginning of 1997.
Dresdner Bank AG, Germany's Number Two commercial bank, ended down 1.05 marks or 1.97 percent at 52.25 marks.
Despite the declines, analysts said the shares were likely to remain underpinned by expectations of an outbreak of merger activity among the big banks in the coming years.
Commerzbank published no other profit figures and analysts said the shortfall from their forecasts may be explained by a bigger-than-expected allocation to bad debt provisions.
That would make sense since company insolvencies are expected to have reached a record high last year.
The bank's nine-month earnings had outshone those of its main rivals due to strong gains in commission and interest income.
Commerzbank said it was allocating 650 million marks of its 1996 net earnings to reserves, up from a transfer of 400 million last year. The total dividend payout for 1996 is 540 million marks.

A spokesman for the bank said in response to a Reuter enquiry that the net profit "roughly" amounted to the sum total of the dividend payout and the allocation to reserves -- 1.19 billion marks -- although the figure was not exact as it it did not contain two smaller items.
Commerzbank also said it had a "good start" in 1997 due in part to favourable capital market conditions.
The bank's group balance sheet total rose by 11.5 percent to 451 billion marks by the end of 1996, driven by a 20 percent jump in lending to 312 billion marks.
The lending rise was caused by increases in lending to local authorities and to banks, Commerzbank said.
